Home version of what we do on the truck, scaled down for two. The thing I keep forgetting at the flat: the wok burner on the truck is 22 kW, the hob in Levenshulme is maybe 3 kW. So cook in batches or it stews.

## The ratio

Per person: 150 g protein, 250 g veg, one portion of rice (water numbers in [[Rice cooker ratios]]).

Sauce is 3:2:1:1 by volume. Light soy, Shaoxing, oyster sauce, sugar syrup (1:1). 60 ml of sauce total for two plates, no more, it's a stir fry not a soup. Cornflour slurry is 1 tsp in 2 tbsp water and only goes in at the very end.

## Prep order

- slice meat against the grain, 5 mm, velvet with 1 tsp bicarb per 250 g for 20 min, rinse, pat dry
- veg cut by cooking time: hard stuff (carrot, broccoli stem) thin, soft stuff (pak choi, beansprouts) big
- aromatics in one pile: 3 cloves garlic, thumb of ginger, 4 spring onion whites
- everything within arm's reach before the gas goes on. No exceptions, Tash.

## Heat and timing

Wok smoking first, then 2 tbsp groundnut oil. Meat in a single layer and leave it 45 seconds before touching it. Out. Veg 2 min. Aromatics 20 s. Meat back, sauce, slurry, plate. Under 6 minutes start to finish. If the pan isn't seasoned right it all welds on, which I sorted in [[Carbon steel wok seasoning]].

## What went wrong, Sept 2024

12 Sept: tried doubling it for Tash and Rob, crammed 600 g chicken thigh in at once, pan temp crashed, grey watery mess. Two batches of 300 g fixed it. Same week I caught my wrist on the wok lip, cold tap for 20 min like [[Burns first aid]] says, blister gone in 4 days.

Macros for Rob who is counting everything this year: about 42 g protein a plate with thigh, he logs it against [[Protein intake]]. Leftovers go straight in the Sunday tubs, see [[Meal prep Sundays]].
